system.name: Shepherd
system.one_liner: a DNN model serving system that makes latency-SLO-aware model provisioning and request scheduling decisions across a GPU cluster

components.name: Request streams
components.role: incoming inference requests for a model and latency SLO, with arbitrary bursty arrival patterns

components.name: Model Serving System
components.role: generic serving system that schedules models and requests onto GPU workers

components.name: Model provision
components.role: decides which models are loaded on which and how many GPUs

components.name: Request Serving
components.role: decides how incoming requests are routed and batched for serving

components.name: GPU Cluster
components.role: the pool of GPU workers that run the served models

components.name: Worker 1
components.role: one GPU worker holding a set of models in GPU memory

components.name: Worker n
components.role: another GPU worker holding a different set of models in GPU memory

content.key_idea: Inference request streams arrive at a model serving system that makes model-provisioning and request-serving decisions to schedule DNN models across workers in a GPU cluster.
content.reading_order: Left to right: Request streams feed the Model Serving System's two decision boxes, which schedule models onto Workers in the GPU Cluster.

style.stroke: ~0.95pt solid strokes on boxes; dashed boxes frame each request-stream chart
style.font: Times New Roman serif, 4-7pt, bold for section titles (Request streams, Model Serving System, GPU Cluster) and box labels
style.arrows: orthogonal arrows with triangular heads; the link from the serving system to the GPU cluster forks into a bidirectional double-headed connector
style.icons: vector: small rate-vs-time charts for each request stream, and simple shapes (rectangle, hexagon, star, triangle) representing individual models in GPU memory

encoding.color_means: orange = Model provision, blue = Request Serving (the two scheduling decision modules); pink/yellow/blue/green shapes = distinct DNN models (M1-M4) resident in a worker's GPU memory; gray header = worker identity bar
encoding.line_style_means: dashed boxes group each request stream's arrival-rate chart; solid arrows show request/decision flow between the three stages
encoding.emphasis: distinct shapes and colors per model (M1...M4) visually convey that many different DNN models can be co-located in one worker's GPU memory, motivating the scheduling problem
reusable_patterns: three-stage input-process-output pipeline (streams -> serving system -> GPU cluster)
small inset charts to characterize input workload shape
weaknesses: model shapes (star, triangle, hexagon) are not explained by any legend beyond the M1..M4 subscript labels
the bidirectional link to workers does not distinguish which direction carries which information

evidence: We focus on Deep Neural Network (DNN) model serving systems
the system makes two scheduling decisions: model provisioning decisions to determine which models should be loaded on which
Figure 1: High-level architecture of model serving system

summary: This figure gives the high-level, generic architecture of a DNN model serving system, used as background before the paper introduces its own system. Multiple request streams, each with its own bursty arrival-rate-over-time pattern, feed into a central Model Serving System. That system makes two kinds of scheduling decisions, shown as an orange 'Model provision' box and a blue 'Request Serving' box: which models to load on which GPUs, and how to route and batch incoming requests. A bidirectional link fans out to a GPU Cluster of workers (Worker 1 ... Worker n), each holding a different set of co-located models in GPU memory, drawn as distinct colored shapes (M1-M4). The figure motivates the joint provisioning-and-serving scheduling problem that the paper's system, Shepherd, is designed to solve.
summary_zh: 该图展示 DNN 模型服务系统的通用高层架构：多路请求流进入服务系统，系统做模型部署与请求调度两类决策，再分发到 GPU 集群中承载不同模型的各个 Worker 上执行。
notes: Figure 1 appears in the Background section as the generic architecture of DNN model serving systems in general, not Shepherd's own novel design (described later), so all components are marked non-novel.
